title: Potato Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage
changes_from_base: Butter-tomato sauce replaced by brown butter with crisp fried sage; gnocchi glazed in the pan.
summary: This follows the same potato gnocchi method as our classic recipe, with the butter-tomato sauce swapped for a simple brown butter and crisp sage glaze.
equipment: 2 baking trays dusted with flour or semolina

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper, King Edward or russet), scrubbed
plain flour, plus extra for dusting
ingredients.note: you may need 10-20 g less or more

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (1%)
ingredients.note: about 6.75 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

steps.title: Bake the potatoes
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, prick the potatoes all over and bake directly on the rack for 50-60 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance. Baking rather than boiling keeps the potato dry, which is what keeps the final dumplings light.

steps.title: Rice the potatoes
steps.text: While still hot, halve the potatoes and scoop the flesh through a ricer onto the worktop in a thin layer, then let it stand for 5 minutes to steam off a little moisture while it's still warm.

steps.title: Bring the dough together
steps.text: Sprinkle over the salt and egg yolk, sieve over two-thirds of the flour and cut it in with a bench scraper. Gather and fold-press the mixture 4-5 times, adding the remaining flour only until it just holds together and feels barely tacky, avoiding kneading or smearing, which would overwork the gluten and make the gnocchi rubbery.

steps.title: Test the dough
steps.text: Boil a single small piece to check it holds together; if it falls apart, fold in another 1-2 tbsp of flour before shaping the rest.

steps.title: Shape the gnocchi
steps.text: Cut the dough into 6 pieces, roll each into a 2cm rope with light hands, then cut into 2cm lengths. Roll each piece down a fork or gnocchi board to leave ridges that will hold the sauce, then lay them on floured trays without touching.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Just before cooking the gnocchi, melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and swirl for 3-4 minutes, until the milk solids turn hazelnut-brown and the butter smells distinctly nutty. Add the sage leaves and fry for 30 seconds until crisp, then lower the heat so the butter doesn't carry on darkening.

steps.title: Cook until they float
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to a rolling boil with the 40g of salt and cook the gnocchi in 2 batches. They're ready when they float, after about 2 minutes, then give them 30 seconds more before lifting them straight into the brown butter with a slotted spoon, keeping a mug of the cooking water.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.text: Add the gnocchi to the brown butter with 2 tbsp of the cooking water and shake the pan over medium heat for 1 minute, so they pick up a light colour at the edges. The added water stops the butter from burning while it forms a light, glossy emulsion around the gnocchi. Season with pepper and serve with Parmesan.

tips: Bake rather than boil the potatoes, exactly as for the classic gnocchi — a wetter potato means more flour and heavier dumplings.
Watch the butter closely once it starts foaming, since brown butter can turn from nutty to burnt within a minute.
Don't skip the splash of cooking water in the final pan — it stops the hot butter from scorching the gnocchi as they glaze.
Keep the gnocchi moving gently in the pan by shaking rather than stirring, so they colour evenly without breaking apart.
storage: Shaped, uncooked gnocchi freeze well on a floured tray for up to 2 months and cook straight from frozen with an extra minute. Cooked gnocchi keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently in a pan until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
